values.name: perUnitBasis
values.value: every quantity as a fraction of its rated-load value: supply voltage 1.00, rated armature current 1.00, rated flux 1.00, rated speed 1.00, rated torque 1.00
values.why: DESIGN CHOICE, not a maker's or a standard's figure. Per-unit means the curves carry no invented motor rating (brief section 9, decision 8). Speed at any armature current is N = [(1 - drop x Ia) / (1 - drop)] / flux, which is speed = (supply - armature-circuit drop) / flux, read off the rated-load point; torque = flux x Ia. Both rules are said on screen.
values.realValueLives: The motor's nameplate and data sheet give the real rated volts, amps, speed and torque.

values.name: ratedArmatureCircuitDrop
values.unit: pu of the supply voltage at rated armature current (armature plus series field)
values.why: EXAMPLE, unsourced. Chosen small, as in lesson 7's shunt set (armature drop 4.0 percent). Used in N = [(1 - 0.05 x Ia) / 0.95] / flux. Label it an example.
values.realValueLives: A winding-resistance test or the maker's data sheet for the real motor (armature and series field resistance).

values.name: noLoadArmatureCurrent
values.why: EXAMPLE, unsourced: the small current that only turns the machine's own friction and iron loss; the same 5 percent as lesson 7's shunt set so the two pictures agree. It is where the left end of each speed curve starts. Armature reaction is ignored and flux is taken as linear in armature current (below saturation), said on screen.
values.realValueLives: A no-load test or the maker's data sheet.

values.name: seriesShareOfFullLoadField
values.value: slider 0 to 100 percent (cumulative); default 15 percent; differential switch limited to 0 to 50 percent
values.unit: percent of the full-load field that the series winding supplies (NEMA's 'percent compounding', source 467)
values.why: EXAMPLE, unsourced. Flux rule shown on screen: cumulative flux = (1 - s) + s x Ia; differential flux = (1 + s) - s x Ia; both equal 1.00 at rated load, so the three machines meet at the rated point. s = 0 is the shunt motor; s = 1 is the series motor (flux = Ia, no shunt part). Default 15 percent is chosen so the COMPUTED speed regulation (22.4 percent, below) sits inside the 15 to 30 percent that Baldor-Reliance gives for standard compound motors (sources 464, 463). Sources disagree on the real share (3 to 10 percent for stabilised shunt, about 50 percent for 'typical industrial', sources 494 and 469); 50 percent would double the no-load speed under this rule (computed: 2.00 pu), so it is NOT used and the disagreement is noted (research.reply.txt, i8 notes).
values.realValueLives: The maker's data sheet or nameplate for the actual motor; NEMA MG 1 defines the term (source 467), the number is the maker's.

values.name: computedSpeedAndTorqueTable
values.why: COMPUTED from the example set above by the two rules; the writer and checker use these to agree on the picture. Series (s=1) speed from the same rule: 21.0 pu at Ia 0.05, 4.16 at 0.25, 2.05 at 0.5, 1.00 at 1.0, 0.47 at 2.0, so the bar goes red (runaway on a light load, source 143/202 family, lesson 6).
values.realValueLives: Recomputed live in the picture; a real motor's curve comes from its test report.

values.name: computedSpeedRegulation
values.value: shunt 5.0 percent; cumulative s=0.15 22.4 percent; cumulative s=0.30 46.9 percent; differential s=0.15 minus 8.1 percent (speed RISES from no load to rated load)
values.unit: percent of rated-load speed (NEMA definition, source 406)
values.why: COMPUTED, (no-load speed - rated-load speed) / rated-load speed with the no-load current above. Teach as a range: makers quote about 30 percent (source 463) and 15 to 25 percent (source 464) for a standard compound; the lesson's 22.4 percent is a computed example, never a maker's figure. His sheet says compound has 'good speed regulation'; the sources say worse than a shunt motor, better than a series motor (contested, noted in research).
values.realValueLives: The maker's data sheet or a no-load against rated-load test.

values.name: startingCurrentLimit
values.unit: pu of rated armature current (200 percent)
values.why: EXAMPLE CHOICE at the top of the cited range: starting resistors typically limit starting current to 125 to 200 percent of full-load current (source 442). With 2.0 pu the starting torque is flux x Ia: shunt 2.00, cumulative (s=0.15) 2.30, cumulative (s=0.30) 2.60, series 4.00, differential (s=0.15) 1.70 pu, in the order the sources give (series highest, compound between, shunt moderate, differential lowest). These are computed, not a maker's starting torque. No maker figure for a compound motor's starting torque as a percent of rated was found (an exam-prep guide's 250 to 300 percent was left out as too weak).
values.realValueLives: The starter maker's data sheet and the motor's data sheet.

values.name: speedRedline
values.why: EXAMPLE limit, unsourced, the same as lesson 7. Where the speed bar turns red; say 'example limit'. A real limit is the 'maximum safe speed' on the nameplate (source 412).
values.realValueLives: The motor's nameplate maximum safe speed.

values.name: differentialFluxZeroCurrent
values.why: COMPUTED: flux (1.15 - 0.15 x Ia) reaches zero at Ia = 1.15 / 0.15. Beyond a few times rated current the picture shows 'flux gone: stalls or reverses' in red, citing the source that a heavy enough load can take the flux to zero (source 474). A real protective device trips long before; the number is only the end of the example curve.
values.realValueLives: Not a design figure; depends on the machine's fields and saturation.

values.name: flywheelEnergyReleased
values.value: falling from the no-load speed to the rated-load speed releases 1 - (N_rated / N_no-load)^2 of the flywheel's stored energy: shunt (5.0 percent droop) 9.3 percent; cumulative s=0.15 (22.4 percent droop) 33.3 percent
values.why: COMPUTED from the cited rule that a flywheel's kinetic energy is proportional to the square of its speed (sources 476 to 478, Yaskawa), applied to the example speeds above. No source says the speed droop is what lets the flywheel give up its energy; say 'worked from the energy rule' and never quote it as a source's statement.
values.realValueLives: The press maker's flywheel data; the motor's data sheet.

values.name: irDropBarOrCurveMagnification
values.why: No magnification is needed: per-unit curves are drawn at true scale. If the writer magnifies any small difference, say so beside it.
values.realValueLives: True scale is the computed table above.
